units.literal: Guan Sheng advised King Han: "Han and Chu have confronted each other at Xingyang for several years. Han has often been in difficulty.

units.zh: 願君王出武關，項王必引兵南走，王深壁，令滎陽成皋間且得休息。
units.en: I ask Your Majesty to go out through Wuguan. Xiang Yu will certainly lead his troops south. Your Majesty should hold deep behind fortifications and let the area between Xingyang and Chenggao gain some respite.
units.literal: I hope your majesty will go out through Wuguan. Xiang Yu will certainly lead troops south. Your majesty should fortify deeply and let the area between Xingyang and Chenggao get some rest.

units.zh: 使韓信等得輯河北趙地，連燕齊，君王乃復走滎陽。
units.en: Let Han Xin and the others consolidate Zhao territory north of the Yellow River and link up with Yan and Qi. Your Majesty can then return to Xingyang.
units.literal: Let Han Xin and others consolidate the lands north of the Yellow River in Zhao, connecting Yan and Qi. Your majesty can then return to Xingyang.

units.zh: 漢王從其計，出軍宛葉間，與黥布行收兵。
units.en: King Han followed his plan, led troops out between Wan and Ye, and together with Ying Bu went to gather troops.
units.literal: King Han followed his plan, led troops out between Wan and Ye, and together with Ying Bu went to gather troops.

units.zh: 羽聞漢王在宛，果引兵南，漢王堅壁不與戰。
units.en: Xiang Yu heard that King Han was at Wan and indeed led troops south. King Han fortified deeply and did not fight him.
units.literal: Xiang Yu heard that King Han was at Wan and indeed led troops south. King Han fortified deeply and did not fight him.

units.zh: 漢王引兵北，擊破終公，復軍成皋。
units.en: King Han led troops north, attacked and defeated Zhong Gong, and returned his army to Chenggao.
units.literal: King Han led troops north, attacked and defeated Zhong Gong, and returned his army to Chenggao.

units.zh: 若非漢王敵也。」
units.en: You are no match for King Han."
units.literal: You are no match for King Han."

units.zh: 漢王跳，獨與滕公共車出成皋玉門，北渡河，宿小脩武。
units.en: The King of Han escaped suddenly, sharing a chariot only with Lord Teng as he left Chenggao by the Jade Gate. They crossed the Yellow River northward and spent the night at Xiao Xiuwu.
units.literal: King Han leapt away, alone with Lord Teng sharing a chariot out of Chenggao's Jade Gate. They crossed north over the Yellow River and stayed at Xiao Xiuwu.

units.zh: 漢王得韓信軍，復大振。
units.en: King Han got Han Xin's army and was greatly strengthened again.
units.literal: King Han got Han Xin's army and was greatly strengthened again.

units.zh: 郎中鄭忠說止漢王，高壘深塹勿戰。
units.en: Attendant Zheng Zhong advised King Han to stop, building high fortifications and deep moats without fighting.
units.literal: Attendant Zheng Zhong advised King Han to stop, building high fortifications and deep moats without fighting.

units.zh: 漢王聽其計，使盧綰、劉賈將卒二萬人，騎數百，渡白馬津入楚地，佐彭越燒楚積聚，復擊破楚軍燕郭西，攻下睢陽、外黃十七城。
units.en: The King of Han followed his plan, sending Lu Wan and Liu Jia with twenty thousand soldiers and several hundred riders across Baima Ford into Chu territory. They assisted Peng Yue in burning Chu's stockpiles, then attacked and defeated the Chu army west of Yanguo, capturing seventeen cities, including Suiyang and Waihuang.
units.literal: King Han followed his plan, sending Lu Wan and Liu Jia with 20,000 troops and several hundred cavalry across Baima ford into Chu territory. They assisted Peng Yue in burning Chu's grain stores, then attacked and broke the Chu army west of Yan Guo, capturing Suiyang and Waihuang, 17 cities.

units.zh: 即漢王欲挑戰，慎勿與戰，勿令得東而已。
units.en: If King Han wants to provoke battle, be careful not to fight him. Just do not let him get east.
units.literal: If King Han wants to provoke battle, be careful not to fight him. Just do not let him get east.

units.zh: 漢王使酈食其說齊王田廣，罷守兵與漢和。
units.en: King Han sent Li Yiji to persuade King Qi Tian Guang to dismiss his guarding troops and make peace with Han.
units.literal: King Han sent Li Yiji to persuade King Qi Tian Guang to dismiss his guarding troops and make peace with Han.

units.zh: 漢王引兵渡河，復取成皋，軍廣武，就敖倉食。
units.en: King Han led troops across the river, recaptured Chenggao, and encamped at Guangwu, drawing provisions from Aocang.
units.literal: King Han led troops across the river, recaptured Chenggao, and encamped at Guangwu, drawing provisions from Aocang.

units.zh: 漢王、羽相與臨廣武之間而語。
units.en: King Han and Xiang Yu faced each other across Guangwu and spoke.
units.literal: King Han and Xiang Yu faced each other across Guangwu and spoke.

units.zh: 羽欲與漢王獨身挑戰，漢王數羽曰：「吾始與羽俱受命懷王，曰先定關中者王之。
units.en: Xiang Yu wanted to challenge the King of Han to single combat. The King of Han instead listed Xiang Yu's crimes: "At first, Xiang Yu and I both received King Huai's command, which said that whoever first pacified Guanzhong would be made king there.
units.literal: Xiang Yu wanted to challenge King Han to single combat. King Han listed Xiang Yu's crimes: "I and Xiang Yu both received commands from King Huai, saying whoever first pacified Guanzhong would be made king.

units.zh: 羽大怒，伏弩射中漢王。
units.en: Xiang Yu was greatly angered and had a crossbow shoot King Han.
units.literal: Xiang Yu was greatly angered and had a crossbow shoot King Han.

units.zh: 漢王傷胸，乃捫足曰：「虜中吾指！」
units.en: King Han was wounded in the chest, but he patted his foot and said: "The bandit hit my toe!"
units.literal: King Han was wounded in the chest, but he patted his foot and said: "The bandit hit my toe!"

units.zh: 漢王病創臥，張良彊請漢王起行勞軍，以安士卒，毋令楚乘勝。
units.en: The King of Han lay ill from his wound. Zhang Liang strongly urged him to get up and go comfort the army, in order to steady the officers and soldiers and not let Chu exploit its victory.
units.literal: King Han lay ill from his wound. Zhang Liang strongly urged King Han to rise and go encourage the troops to stabilize the soldiers and officers, not letting Chu take advantage of their victory.

units.zh: 漢王出行軍，疾甚，因馳入成皋。
units.en: King Han went out to encourage the troops, but his illness was severe, so he galloped into Chenggao.
units.literal: King Han went out to encourage the troops, but his illness was severe, so he galloped into Chenggao.

units.zh: 漢王疾瘉，西入關，至櫟陽，存問父老，置酒。
units.en: King Han recovered from his illness, entered the passes to the west, reached Queyang, visited the elders, and held a banquet.
units.literal: King Han recovered from his illness, entered the passes to the west, reached Queyang, visited the elders, and held a banquet.

units.zh: 漢王怒，欲攻之。
units.en: King Han was angry and wanted to attack him.
units.literal: King Han was angry and wanted to attack him.

units.zh: 漢王下令：軍士不幸死者，吏為衣衾棺斂，轉送其家。
units.en: King Han issued an order: For soldiers who unfortunately die, officials shall provide burial clothes, coffins, and shrouds, and transport them home.
units.literal: King Han issued an order: For soldiers who unfortunately die, officials shall provide burial clothes, coffins, and shrouds, and transport them home.

units.zh: 漢王欲西歸，張良、陳平諫曰：「今漢有天下太半，而諸侯皆附，楚兵罷食盡，此天亡之時，不因其幾而遂取之，所謂養虎自遺患也。」
units.en: The King of Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised him: "Han now possesses more than half the realm, and all the feudal lords have attached themselves to it. Chu's troops are exhausted and its food is gone. This is the moment when Heaven is destroying Chu. If we do not seize this opportunity and take it, that is what is called raising a tiger and leaving disaster for oneself."
units.literal: King Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised: "Now Han possesses more than half the world, and all the feudal lords are attached. Chu troops are exhausted and food is finished. This is the time Heaven has doomed them. If we do not take advantage of this opportunity to destroy them, this is called raising a tiger that brings disaster to oneself."

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 孝文時，吳太子入見，得侍皇太子飲博。
units.en: In Emperor Wen’s reign the crown prince of Wu attended court and was allowed to drink and play liubo with the imperial heir.
units.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen the Wu heir came to court and was admitted to drink and play liubo with the heir apparent.

units.zh: 博爭道，不恭，皇太子引博局提吳太子，殺之。
units.en: They quarreled over the rules; the Wu heir showed disrespect, and the crown prince seized the heavy board and struck him dead.
units.literal: A dispute over a move in the game turned disrespectful; the imperial heir snatched up the gaming board and dashed it against the Wu prince, killing him.

units.zh: 朝錯為太子家令，得幸皇太子，數從容言吳過可削。
units.en: Chao Cuo was serving as household steward to the crown prince and had won his favor. He repeatedly said in private that Wu's offenses gave grounds for reducing its territory.
units.literal: Chao Cuo served as household steward to the crown prince. Favored by the crown prince, he repeatedly said in private that Wu's offenses could be grounds for reducing its territory.

units.zh: 及景帝即位，錯為御史大夫，說上曰：「昔高帝初定天下，昆弟少，諸子弱，大封同姓，故孽子悼惠王王齊七十二城，庶弟元王王楚四十城，兄子王吳五十餘城。
units.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo became Imperial Counselor. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, he had few brothers and his sons were young, so he gave large fiefs to men of his own surname. Thus King Daohui, his son by a concubine, ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; King Yuan, his younger half-brother, ruled Chu with forty cities; and his nephew ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, Cuo became Grandee Secretary. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, his brothers were few and his sons were young, so he made large grants to men of his own surname. Thus King Daohui, his son by a concubine, ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; King Yuan, his younger half-brother, ruled Chu with forty cities; and his elder brother's son ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.

units.zh: 孝景前三年正月甲子，初起兵於廣陵。
units.en: On jiǎzǐ in the first month of Xiaojing’s third year the rebellion opened at Guangling.
units.literal: On the jiǎzǐ day of the first month in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing, he first raised troops at Guangling.

units.zh: 七國反書聞，天子乃遣太尉條侯周亞夫將三十六將軍往擊吳楚；
units.en: News of the seven kingdoms’ revolt reached court; the emperor sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu of Tiaohou with thirty-six generals against Wu and Chu;
units.literal: When word of the seven states' rebellion reached the throne, the Son of Heaven dispatched Grand Commandant Marquis of Tiaohou Zhou Yafu with thirty-six generals to strike Wu and Chu;

units.zh: 陛下多病志逸，不能省察。
units.en: The Son of Heaven is sick in body and distracted in will; he cannot see through the plot.
units.literal: The sovereign is often ill in mind and body and cannot look into these matters.

units.zh: 二月，吳王兵既破，敗走，於是天子制詔將軍：「蓋聞為善者天報以福，為非者天報以殃。
units.en: In the second month Wu’s army was shattered; the emperor told his generals: “Heaven crowns virtue with fortune and strikes evil with woe.
units.literal: In the second month the King of Wu's army had already been broken and fled in defeat; the Son of Heaven then issued an edict to the generals: “We have heard that Heaven rewards the good with blessing and the wicked with calamity.

units.zh: 王頓首膝行對曰：「今者，朝錯天子用事臣，變更高皇帝法令，侵奪諸侯地。
units.en: On his knees Ang said, “Chao Cuo rules the court, rewrites Gaozu’s statutes, and gnaws at princely fiefs.
units.literal: The king, knocking his head and crawling on his knees, replied, “At present Chao Cuo is the minister in charge at the Son of Heaven's side; he has altered the laws of the August Emperor Gaozu and seized the princes' lands.

units.zh: 又使使愬條侯於上，上使告條侯救梁，又守便宜不行。
units.en: They complained to the throne; the emperor told him to relieve Liang, yet he clung to his plan and stayed put.
units.literal: They also sent envoys to denounce Zhou Yafu to the emperor; the emperor ordered him to save Liang, yet he still held to tactical advantage and did not move.

units.zh: 及後使人為秋請，上復責問吳使者。
units.en: Later, when Wu sent an envoy for the autumn audience, the emperor again questioned and rebuked him.
units.literal: Later, when Wu sent a man for the autumn audience, the emperor again questioned and rebuked the Wu envoy.

units.zh: 於是天子皆赦吳使者歸之，而賜吳王几杖，老，不朝。
units.en: The Son of Heaven pardoned the envoys and sent them back, then gave the king of Wu a folding stool and staff in token of old age, freeing him from court calls.
units.literal: The emperor pardoned Wu’s envoys and sent them home, then bestowed on the king of Wu an arm-rest and staff as tokens of age, exempting him from court attendance.

units.zh: 遣曲周侯酈寄擊趙，將軍欒布擊齊，大將軍竇嬰屯滎陽監齊趙兵。
units.en: he sent Li Ji, marquis of Quzhou, against Zhao and Luan Bu against Qi, while Grand General Dou Ying encamped at Xingyang to keep watch over the armies of Qi and Zhao.
units.literal: he sent Marquis Li Ji of Quzhou against Zhao and General Luan Bu against Qi; Grand General Dou Ying encamped at Xingyang to keep watch over the Qi and Zhao armies.

units.zh: 上從其議，遂斬錯。
units.en: The emperor accepted his counsel and had Chao Cuo executed.
units.literal: The emperor accepted his counsel and had Chao Cuo executed.

units.zh: 高皇帝親垂功德，建立諸侯，幽王、悼惠王絕無後，孝文皇帝哀憐加惠，王幽王子遂，悼惠王子卬等，令奉其先王宗廟，為漢藩國，德配天地，明並日月。
units.en: Gaozu established the kingdoms. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off, Emperor Wen compassionately made You’s son Sui, Daohui’s son Ang, and others kings so that they could tend their forefathers’ shrines and serve as Han’s outer bulwarks. His virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.
units.literal: The August Emperor Gaozu personally bestowed merit and virtue by establishing the princes. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off without successors, Emperor Xiaowen took pity and extended his grace, making King You's son Sui, King Daohui's son Ang, and others kings so that they could maintain their forefathers' ancestral temples and serve as Han's outer bulwarks—his virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.

units.zh: 而吳王濞背德反義，誘受天下亡命罪人，亂天下幣，稱疾不朝二十餘年。
units.en: Yet Liu Bi spurned virtue, drew in fugitives, disrupted the currency, and for more than twenty years pleaded illness and stayed away from court.
units.literal: Yet the King of Wu Liu Bi turned his back on virtue and violated righteousness, enticed and harbored fugitive criminals from the realm, threw the realm's currency into confusion, and for more than twenty years claimed illness and did not attend court.

units.zh: 有司數請濞罪，孝文皇帝寬之，欲其改行為善。
units.en: Officials begged his head; Wendi spared him, hoping he would mend his ways.
units.literal: The authorities repeatedly requested Bi's punishment; Emperor Xiaowen was lenient and wished him to change his conduct for the good.

units.zh: 今乃與楚王戊、趙王遂、膠西王卬、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、膠東王雄渠約從謀反，為逆無道，起兵以危宗廟，賊殺大臣及漢使者，迫劫萬民，伐殺無罪，燒殘民家，掘其丘壟，甚為虐暴。
units.en: Now he has allied with Liu Wu of Chu, Liu Sui of Zhao, Liu Ang of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang of Jinan, Liu Xian of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong to plot rebellion. These lawless traitors menace the temples, murder ministers and envoys, coerce the people, kill the innocent, burn their homes, and dig open their graves. Their cruelty is monstrous.
units.literal: Now he has joined with Liu Wu, king of Chu, Liu Sui, king of Zhao, Liu Ang, king of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang, king of Jinan, Liu Xian, king of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu, king of Jiaodong, in an alliance to plot rebellion. Lawless in their treason, they raised troops to endanger the ancestral temples, murdered great ministers and Han envoys, coerced the people, slaughtered the innocent, burned commoners' homes, and dug open their tombs—utterly cruel and violent.

units.zh: 而卬等又重逆無道，燒宗廟，鹵御物，朕甚痛之。
units.en: Ang’s crew have burned the shrines and plundered the palace stores—Our heart is torn.
units.literal: Yet Ang and the others have again been utterly lawless, burned the temples, looted the imperial gear—the pain of this is great in Us.

units.zh: 朕素服避正殿，將軍其勸士大夫擊反虜。
units.en: We wear mourning and quit the main hall—generals, drive your men at the traitors.
units.literal: We have donned plain dress and avoided the main hall; generals, urge your officers to strike the rebels.

units.zh: 擊反虜者，深入多殺為功，斬首捕虜比三百石以上皆殺，無有所置。
units.en: Advance deep and kill many to earn merit; execute every captured rebel of three-hundred-picul rank or higher, sparing none.
units.literal: Those who strike the rebels shall take deep advances and heavy killing as merit; every captured rebel of the three-hundred-picul rank or above shall be put to death, with none spared.

units.zh: 敢有議詔及不如詔者，皆要斬。」
units.en: Debate the decree or disobey it—death by waist chop.”
units.literal: Whoever dares debate the edict or fail to match the edict—waist cut in two.”

units.zh: 高曰：「御史大夫朝錯熒惑天子，侵奪諸侯，蔽忠塞賢，朝廷疾怨，諸侯皆有背叛之意，人事極矣。
units.en: Ying Gao said, “Grandee Secretary Chao Cuo dazzles the Son of Heaven, strips the feudatories, blocks the loyal and worthy, so that the court boils with anger and every prince nurses rebellion. The crisis is complete.
units.literal: Gao answered, “Grandee Secretary Chao Cuo dazzles the sovereign, carves up the princes, silences loyal men and worthy advisors, until both court and kingdoms seethe with resentment and every prince harbors thoughts of revolt. Human patience is stretched to the limit.

units.zh: 召入見，上問以吳楚之計，盎對曰：「吳楚相遺書，曰『賊臣朝錯擅適諸侯，削奪之地』，以故反，名為西共誅錯，復故地而罷。
units.en: Yuan Ang was summoned to audience, and the emperor asked him about the plans of Wu and Chu. Ang replied, "Wu and Chu have exchanged letters saying, 'The wicked minister Chao Cuo has arbitrarily punished the feudal lords and stripped away their lands.' That is why they have rebelled. Their stated aim is to march west together, execute Chao Cuo, restore their former territories, and then disband.
units.literal: Ang was summoned to audience. The emperor asked him about the Wu-Chu situation. Ang replied, "Wu and Chu have sent each other messages saying, 'The wicked minister Chao Cuo has wantonly punished the feudal lords and seized their lands.' For this reason they have rebelled, claiming to execute Chao Cuo together from the west and then restore their former territories and disband.

units.zh: 久之，王問仲舒曰：「粵王勾踐與大夫洩庸、種、蠡謀伐吳，遂滅之。
units.en: One day the king asked, "Goujian of Yue and his ministers Xie Yong, Wen Zhong, and Fan Li destroyed Wu by counsel.
units.literal: After a long time the king asked Zhongshu, saying: "The Yue king Goujian, with his great officers Xie Yong, Zhong, and Li, plotted to attack Wu and thereby destroyed it.

units.zh: 會呂嘉反，式上書曰：「臣聞主愧臣死。
units.en: When Lü Jia rose in the south, Bu Shi wrote: "They say when the sovereign is shamed his servants must die.
units.literal: When Lü Jia rebelled, Shi submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that when the ruler is ashamed the minister dies.

units.zh: 而御史大夫張湯方貴用事，減宣、杜周等為中丞，義縱、尹齊、王溫舒等用急刻為九卿，直指夏蘭之屬始出。
units.en: At this time the Censor-in-Chief Zhang Tang was powerful and in charge of affairs. Jian Xuan and Du Zhou served as Palace Assistant Censors; Yi Zong, Yin Qi, Wang Wenshu, and others, who used harsh severity, became Nine Ministers; and direct investigators such as Xia Lan first appeared.
units.literal: At this time Censor-in-chief Zhang Tang was in power; Jian Xuan and Du Zhou served as deputy censors; Yi Zong, Yin Qi, and Wang Wenshu, who used harsh severity, became among the Nine Ministers; direct investigators such as Xia Lan first appeared.

units.zh: 及王恢謀馬邑，匈奴絕和親，侵優北邊，兵連而不解，天下共其勞。
units.en: When Wang Hui plotted at Mayi, the Xiongnu broke off the marriage alliance, raided and harassed the northern frontier; warfare continued without end, and all under heaven shared the burden.
units.literal: When Wang Hui plotted at Mayi, the Xiongnu broke off marriage alliance, raided and harassed the northern frontier, warfare continued without end, and all under heaven shared the burden.

units.zh: 歷觀前古，鑒之往事，子陽、季孟，傾覆相尋，餘善、
units.en: Looking through antiquity and taking mirror from past affairs, Ziyang, Jimeng, overturn followed in succession; Yu Shan and
units.literal: Looking through former antiquity and taking mirror from past affairs, Ziyang, Jimeng, overturn followed in succession; Yu Shan and

units.zh: 沈炯 虞荔 弟寄 馬樞
units.en: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
units.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

units.zh: 梁使韓安國及楚死事相弟張羽為將軍，乃得頗敗吳兵。
units.en: Only when Liang made Han Anguo and Zhang Yu—the younger brother of Chu’s chancellor, who had died in service—generals could it begin to defeat Wu’s troops.
units.literal: Liang then made Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, younger brother of Chu's chancellor who had died in service, generals; only then were they able to inflict some defeats on the Wu army.

units.zh: 於是諸侯上疏曰：「楚王韓信、韓王信、淮南王英布、梁王彭越、故衡山王吳芮、趙王張敖、燕王臧荼昧 死再拜言，大王陛下：先時秦為亡道，天下誅之。
units.en: So the feudal lords submitted a memorial: "Han Xin, King of Chu; Xin, King of Han; Ying Bu, King of Huainan; Peng Yue, King of Liang; Wu Rui, former King of Hengshan; Zhang Ao, King of Zhao; and Zang Tu, King of Yan, risking death, bow twice and say: Great King, Your Majesty, formerly Qin acted without the Way, and the world punished it.
units.literal: So the feudal lords submitted a memorial: "King of Chu Han Xin, King of Han Xin, King of Huainan Ying Bu, King of Liang Peng Yue, former King of Hengshan Wu Rui, King of Zhao Zhang Ao, King of Yan Zang Tu, risking death, bow twice and say: Great King Your Majesty, previously Qin acted without righteousness, the world executed it.

units.zh: 詔曰：「故衡山王吳芮與子二人、兄子一人，從百粵之兵，以佐諸侯，誅暴秦，有大功，諸侯立以為王。
units.en: The edict said: "The former King of Hengshan, Wu Rui, with two sons and one nephew, led Baiyue troops to assist the feudal lords in punishing the violent Qin and had great merit. The feudal lords established him as king.
units.literal: The edict said: "The former King of Hengshan Wu Rui, with two sons and one nephew, led Baiyue troops to assist the feudal lords, executed the violent Qin, had great merit. The feudal lords established him as king.

units.zh: 項羽侵奪之地，謂之番君。
units.en: Xiang Yu invaded and seized his territory, calling him Fan Jun.
units.literal: Xiang Yu invaded and seized his territory, calling him Fan Jun.

units.zh: 其以長沙、豫章、象郡、桂林、南海立番君芮為長沙王。」
units.en: Enfeoff Fan Jun Wu Rui as King of Changsha with Changsha, Yuzhang, Xiangjun, Guilin, and Nanhai."
units.literal: Enfeoff Fan Jun Wu Rui as King of Changsha with Changsha, Yuzhang, Xiangjun, Guilin, and Nanhai."

units.zh: 楊僕，宜陽人也。
units.en: Yang Pu came from Yiyang.
units.literal: Yang Pu was a man of Yiyang.

units.zh: 僕惶恐，對曰：「願盡死贖罪！」
units.en: Yang Pu stammered, "I will spend my life paying for these crimes!"
units.literal: Pu trembling replied: "Willing to exhaust death redeeming crime!"

units.zh: 南越反，拜為樓船將軍，有功，封將梁侯。
units.en: He commanded the tower-ship fleet against Southern Yue and won the marquisate of Jiangliang.
units.literal: Southern Yue rebelled—appointed tower-ship general—had merit—enfeoffed General Liang marquis.

units.zh: 還，免為庶人，病死。
units.en: Stripped of rank, he died a commoner.
units.literal: Returned—stripped to commoner—died of illness.

units.zh: 東越反，上欲復使將，為其伐前勞，以書敕責之曰：「將軍之功，獨有先破石門、尋狹，非有斬將騫旗之實也，烏足以驕人哉！
units.en: Planning a second campaign, the emperor sent a blistering edict: "General, your merit lies only in being first to break Shimen and Xinxia—you have no record of beheading enemy commanders or seizing their banners. How can that suffice to swagger before others?
units.literal: Eastern Yue rebelled—the sovereign wished to employ him again—because he boasted prior labor—with document rebuked saying: "General's merit—only first breaking Shimen and Xinxia—not having beheaded a general or seized banners—how enough to pride yourself before others!
